decisive_spans.text: a 17 × 9 cm mixed solid and cystic mass occupying the right hepatic lobe with compression of the inferior vena cava (IVC)
An 8-year-old girl weighing 44.5 kg with no significant medical history presented with a 1-week history of progressive abdominal pain, distension, nausea, and vomiting

response.rationale: The vignette describes a large hepatic mass in a child with progressive abdominal pain and vascular complications, which strongly supports Hepatoblastoma. While Inferior Vena Cava Thrombosis and Pulmonary Embolism are present, they are complications of the underlying hepatic mass, not the primary diagnosis. Abdominal compartment syndrome is also a complication.
